newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan credit banks reveal BIS ratio, latent profit.
newsitem.headline: Japan credit banks reveal BIS ratio, latent profit.

text.p: Japan's three long-term credit banks on Monday disclosed capital adequacy ratios and unrealised profits on their shareholdings as of September 30.
The three banks are the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ), the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB) and Nippon Credit Bank Ltd.
Capital adequacy ratios with comparisons for March:
Under rules set by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), Japanese banks operating internationally must have capital equivalent to eight percent of risk-weighted assets.
Japan allows banks to include unrealised profits on shareholdings as part of capital.
